I am old and I have not studied, so I do not count things like the technicians do. I look at what people around me do and I keep it steady. I only farm 6 mu, and some people in my house work outside, so I cannot spread money everywhere. This year I will keep most land in the usual wheat-maize rotation because that is the safest for grain and cash. I will leave a smaller part for cotton and a little stevia to try for some extra money, but I will not put too much land there because I am still new at this and I do not want one bad crop to drag the whole family down. Since I have a well, I will water when the crop really needs it, but not too many times because pumping costs money.

For area, I will use 3 mu for wheat followed by summer maize on the same 3 mu. I will keep 2 mu in cotton and 1 mu in stevia. For fertilizer, I will not go too light because if the crop turns weak, the yield loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. But I also will not chase very high rates. I will use round, familiar amounts, mostly base fertilizer plus one or two topdressings. If pests are light, I spray once; if not, I spray again. I depend mostly on family labor, and if the wheat harvest and maize sowing are too rushed, I will hire a little machine or labor for those few days.
